newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Oct current account surplus down 19.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Japan Oct current account surplus down 19.6 pct.

text.p: Japan's current account surplus, the broadest measure of trade in goods and services, dropped 19.6 percent in October from a year earlier to 367.4 billion yen, the Finance Ministry announced on Wednesday.
The average of economists' forecasts had been a fall of about 9.6 percent in October from a year earlier to 413.1 billion yen.
The figures are released in yen. At Wednesday morning's exchange rate of about 113 yen to the dollar, October's current account surplus was $3.25 billion.
The current account surplus has been falling on a year-on-year basis every month since December 1994. It totalled 457.1 billion yen ($4.04 billion) in October 1995.
The year-on-year drop in September was 35.6 percent. Economists had expected the pace of the drop to slow in October, due mainly to a slight fall in the trade surplus that month.
The overall trade surplus fell 12.9 percent in October from a year earlier to 470.86 billion yen ($4.16 billion), the 23rd consecutive month it has declined on a year-on-year basis.
